title: CBRU at MMN 2026 in Bari, Italy
content:
CBRU researchers contributed to the scientific programme through a keynote talk, symposium presentations, and poster presentations.

Research Director Mari Tervaniemi delivered a keynote talk titled “MMN and prediction and beyond?”

Dr. Paula Virtala (CBRU) organized a symposium titled “Mismatch responses as neural markers of speech processing in typically developing and at-risk children”, featuring presentations by Dr. Sergio Navarrete Arroyo (CBRU), Associate Professor Sari Ylinen (University of Tampere), and Liis Themas (University of Tartu).

Professor Minna Huotilainen contributed to the scientific programme with a talk titled “The developing musical brain: Past, present, and future of infant music neuroscience”.

In addition to presenting their own research, Professor Minna Huotilainen and University lecturer Petri Paavilainen chaired scientific sessions featuring presentations by other researchers.

CBRU was also represented by researchers at different career stages who presented their work through poster presentations: Xiazhen Liu, Beatrice Aquilino, Emilia Takaluoma, Dr. Sergio Navarrete Arroyo, Dr. Peixin Nie, and University lecturer Petri Paavilainen.

title: Hanlin Yu väittelee aiheesta Jakaumien ja mallien vertailu: Geometria ja tiheyssuhteet
content:
M.Sc. Hanlin Yu defends his PhD thesis “Comparing Distributions and Models: Geometry and Density Ratios ” on Friday the 20th of September 2026 at 13 in the University of Helsinki Physicum Building, Auditorium E204 (Gustaf Hällströmin katu 2, 2nd floor). His opponent is Reader Andrew B. Duncan (Imperial College London, United Kingdom) and custos Professor Arto Klami (University of Helsinki). The defence will be held in English.

The thesis of Hanlin Yu is a part of research done in the Department of Computer Science and in the Multi-source Probabilistic Inference group at the University of Helsinki. His supervisors have been Professor Arto Klami and Academy Research Fellow Marcelo Hartmann (University of Helsinki).

title: Urbaria Guest Lecture with Professor Alistair Fraser
content:
Date: 23 November 2026
Time: 16.15-17.45
Place: B212 (room 2), Metsätalo (Unioninkatu 40, Helsinki)
 
Gangs and the Gig Economy: Violence, New Media and the Street Field
Alistair Fraser
 
Abstract
Highly visible, street-based groups of young people, engaging in crime or violent conflict, have been reported in spaces of advanced marginality throughout the world and in many cases, these forms of identification have long historical antecedents, with marked continuities over time and space. This has led to conceptualisations, drawing on Bourdieu, of a ‘street field’ in which criminal actors enter into struggle for resources in the form of ‘street capital’. As in other field environments, however, the ‘rules of the game’ within the street field are subject to change (Bourdieu 2017). Recent scholarship has, for example, drawn attention to a range of external causes for change in the nature and texture of ‘road capitals’ (Bakkali 2022) within the street field – including the impact of digital street culture (Lane 2019), shifting patterns of drug distribution (Bakken et al 2023), and the fragmentation of territorial identity (Aspholm 2020). In this paper, drawing on a longitudinal ethnography of young people’s ‘gang’ identification in Glasgow, Scotland, I trace the shifting dynamics of violence against a backdrop of social change. Where the drivers of street violence among young people were once found in neighbourhood disputes, the roots of such conflicts now exist across virtual and physical boundaries amid increased precarity in both the licit and illicit economies – prompting new questions for the nature and meaning of ‘gang’ identity in the digital age. 
 
Bio
Alistair Fraser is Professor of Criminology at the University of Glasgow, where he teaches and researches issues of youth violence, street culture, and urban crime, with an abiding interest in the global gang phenomenon. 
 
The following speakers will provide brief comments after the presentation:
Kimmo Nuotio, Professor of Criminal Law and the Director of the Institute of Criminology and Legal Policy
David Inglis, Professor of Sociology
Juuda Tamminen, PhD student, researcher on project ”The Moral Drama of Street Gangs. A multidimensional approach to the ”gang problem” in Finland”

After the lecture, we invite you to stay for a glass of wine and a chance to talk with the speakers and other participants.

title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu tammikuussa – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots en Route
content:
Plants have always travelled – with the wind, with animals and birds, with humans. They have been carried across oceans, taken from their habitats and replanted to serve trade and empire.

Roots en Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: ANEE+ employed researchers starting work
content: The call for applications for postdoctoral and university researcher positions in the study of ancient Near East received a large number of high-quality proposals. The ANEE+ management team is excited to announce that Emanuel Pfoh and Melis Uzdurum were chosen for university researcher positions, and Ellie Bennett and Richard Bott for postdoctoral researcher positions. These four new hires strengthen the role of ancient Near Eastern studies at the University of Helsinki and further the goals of the ANEE+ Interdisciplinary Research Network.
